# AHU-3 Sequence of Operation: Review Findings

I reviewed only the text you pasted. Severity: **A** = life safety or code, resolve before programming. **B** = will cause control or comfort failures. **C** = completeness or testability.

## A. Safety and code

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-01 | Step 5 (FZ-3) | Auto restart at a temperature rise defeats the freezestat. The unit can cycle into a freeze condition. No coil protection is defined: HV-3 position, pump command, and CV-3 position are missing. | Make FZ-3 hardwired to the starter, with manual reset. On trip, command HV-3 open, run the heating pump, and close the OA damper. Ask the engineer whether freeze risk in Houston justifies the device. If it does, they must define the full response. |
| R-02 | Step 6 (SD-3) | "Stops SF-3 through the BAS" makes life-safety shutdown depend on software. Restart needs only a BAS acknowledgment, with no reset at the detector or fire alarm panel. | Hardwire SD-3 to the SF-3 starter or VFD safety input. Report the status to the BAS and the fire alarm panel. Require reset at the source before any restart. Confirm the NFPA 90A and AHJ requirements and the smoke damper interface. |
| R-03 | Step 7 | "Valves stay in last position" is not a fail position. A frozen heating valve or open cooling valve after power loss is undefined. Restart behavior is missing: auto or manual, delays, and the start order of damper, fan, and valves. | Define the fail position per device (HV-3, CV-3, OA damper) by tag. Define the power-restart sequence with its delays. Make the actuator spec match (spring return or not). |
| R-04 | Whole document | No high-static cutout is defined, and no fan-status proof (SF-3 status or DP switch). | Add a hardwired high-static trip and a fan-proving step with a timeout and failure response. |

## B. Control logic and the Houston climate

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-05 | Step 3 | A 75 F dry-bulb economizer limit is wrong for a hot, humid climate. Outdoor air at 75 F with high humidity adds a large latent load. No enthalpy or dewpoint limit is given. | Use an enthalpy or dewpoint high limit, and give the limit as a value in a setpoint list. Confirm that an economizer is useful here at all. |
| R-06 | Steps 1, 3 | Lab AHUs normally supply 100% OA with no recirculation, and air change rates come from the lab ventilation design. A 20% minimum OA and a mixed-air economizer suggest a template sequence. | Ask the engineer: is AHU-3 100% OA or mixed air? If 100% OA, delete the economizer and minimum OA. If mixed air, state the return air path and the lab exhaust and pressurization requirements. |
| R-07 | Steps 3, 4 | The MAT setpoint equals the DAT setpoint. At mid-range OAT (for example 70 F), a mixed-air setpoint of 55 F cannot be reached, so the damper saturates open. No OA damper control is defined for when the economizer is off. | Define the economizer enable and disable logic and the damper position outside the economizer range. Separate the MAT control from the DAT control. |
| R-08 | Step 4 | No dehumidification control. A fixed 55 F DAT with no humidity reset, no reheat logic, and no space or return humidity input risks high humidity (mold risk). One PID output with a 0–50 / 50–100 split also has no deadband, so heating and cooling can hunt. | Add a humidity control loop and reheat logic. Define a deadband and the heating and cooling interaction. Change the split to a setpoint list entry. |
| R-09 | Step 2 | No upper space temperature or humidity limit when unoccupied. Humidity can run away overnight in Houston. The heating call uses a space temperature that is not tagged, and no stop condition or minimum run time is given. With the OA damper closed, lab exhaust can drive the space negative. | Add unoccupied cooling and humidity limits. Name the sensor tag. Define the stop condition (hysteresis) and minimum run time. Confirm the exhaust and pressurization requirements. |
| R-10 | Step 1 | The fixed static setpoint has no reset. Where DPT-3 is located is not stated. The occupied schedule is hard-coded in prose, and labs are often occupied 24/7 at reduced air change rates. | Add a static pressure reset strategy and the sensor tag. Move the schedule to a list. Confirm the lab occupancy and setback requirements. |
| R-11 | Steps 1, 5 | Start and stop sequences are missing: damper-open-before-fan-start, a proof timeout, the fan ramp, and the shutdown order. | Add a step table: Step, Action, Transition condition, Timeout, Failure response. |

## C. Completeness and testability

| ID | Location | Issue | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| R-12 | Whole document | No requirement IDs and no test method for each requirement (FR-AHU3-NNN). | Assign IDs and add a FAT test for each. |
| R-13 | Steps 1–5 | Numbers sit in prose: 1.5 in. w.c., 20%, 55 F, 60 F, 75 F, 38 F, 40 F, 06:00–18:00, 0/50/100%. | Move them to one setpoint list and reference it. |
| R-14 | Whole document | No bad-PV, comms-loss, or sensor-failure handling. | Define the behavior for each PV: DAT, MAT, OAT, DPT-3, space temperature. |
| R-15 | Whole document | No states or transitions table (occupied, unoccupied, freeze, smoke, fault, restart). No operator interface, alarm reference, or filter status. | Build the state table first, with permissives and exits. Reference the alarm database. |
| R-16 | Whole document | Most devices have no tags: temperature and pressure sensors, OA damper, and the space sensor. The writing is not STE (for example "stops through the BAS"). | Reference the instrument index. Apply an STE pass after the content is settled. |
| R-17 | Whole document | No open items list with owner and date. | Log R-01 to R-16 as open items. Suggested owners: the mechanical engineer for R-05 to R-10, the controls lead for R-11 to R-16, and the fire protection engineer for R-02. |

## Suggested RFI to the engineer (priority order)
1. Is AHU-3 100% OA or mixed air? (R-06)
2. Fire alarm and smoke detector shutdown wiring, plus the freezestat reset method (R-01, R-02)
3. Actuator fail positions and power-restart behavior (R-03)
4. Humidity control and the economizer limit (R-05, R-08)
5. Occupancy schedule and unoccupied limits (R-09, R-10)

I did not verify code citations or the project documents (the cause-and-effect chart, the instrument index, and the setpoint list), so check those against your project submittals.
